subject.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins

question: Should the canonical fix be this broader branch or the proof-positive implementation in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063?
rationale: Both branches address the same destructive failure path, but this PR includes additional parser coverage while the competing PR has stronger live behavior proof; repository history alone does not choose which branch should own the final contract.

options.title: Consolidate into PR 107063
options.body: Use the proof-positive narrower branch and port the singleton-array update-check change if current main still requires it.

options.title: Consolidate into this PR
options.body: Keep this broader branch, add a live exact-head CLI state transition, and close the competing branch after confirming equivalent coverage.

options.title: Pause both branches
options.body: Hold both implementations until the update-path owner confirms the permanent classification contract for non-E404 metadata failures.

recommendation.title: Consolidate into PR 107063
recommendation.body: Use the proof-positive narrower branch and port the singleton-array update-check change if current main still requires it.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied feature history connects this person to both the update-check parser and destructive plugin update-failure policy.
